Resolves #18874

The Animate plugin's measured mode gave a uniform row **pitch** and content-height **items**, so mixed content floated in tall slots. Every item now takes the row height, exactly like a fixed-mode item. The plugin can write that height only because it no longer measures through a plain rect read: `Neo.main.DomAccess.getNaturalRect()` lifts the named inline style properties off every node, reads every layout box and restores the values — one synchronous task, one forced layout for any number of nodes. `component.Base#getNaturalRect` is the App Worker shortcut beside `getDomRect` / `getLayoutRect`.

Evidence: L3 (real browser — the component tier and `examples/list/animate` served from this branch) → L3 required (AC-1, AC-2, AC-5). Residual: none.

agent-preflight: not hosted here; the baseline jobs run in CI. Declared class: `capability` → `feat` (a new remote read and its component shortcut).

## Deltas from ticket

- **The read answers the layout box, not the visual rect.** What comes back is written into a CSS `height`, so it has to be layout px; `getBoundingClientRect` is post-transform, and an animated ancestor (a dock FLIP window) would scale it. `measureRows` read visual rects before — that goes with this change.
- **A sibling of the rect reads, not an overload of `measure`.** `measure` converts one CSS *length* to px for one node and returns a Number; this read returns the rects of many nodes, and batching is its point (release all → read all → restore all, or every item costs a layout). `measure` also has an open defect and no engine caller (#18881) — not a base to build on. @tobiu named the overload as viable; these are the reasons it is not the shape here.
- `properties` is a parameter (default `['height']`): width is the same trap at no extra code.
- **The trap was worse than the ticket said.** Not grow-only: an element with an inline `height` answers a rect read with that height whatever its content does, so a naive write-back freezes the row at its first measurement. The ticket body is corrected; the mutation receipts below are where it showed.
- `createItem` lost its mode branch: `rowHeight` alone decides between "fill the row" and "hidden, content-tall". `repositionItems` writes the row height in both modes (fixed mode: the value it already carried).
- Accretion: the consumer-side deletion is `neomjs/neo-agent-institution#128` — the roster's `itemHeight: 126` anatomy constant and its docblock go once a pin carries this.

### 🧭 Patch-Blind Premise Snapshot

*   **Inputs Read Before Patch:**
    - #18874 with its options table and Contract Ledger.
    - `list.plugin.Animate` at head: `createItem`, `repositionItems`, `measureRows`, the `rowHeight` getter.
    - The per-owner transition rule `getOwnerRules()` inserts: `opacity` and `transform` only.
    - The construct-time guard that reports an owner with neither `itemHeight` nor `measureItemHeight`.
    - `DomAccess#getLayoutRect` / `getBoundingClientRect` as siblings, and `component.Base#getDomRect` / `getLayoutRect` as the shortcut pattern.
*   **Expected Solution Shape:** Option B. A main-thread read that releases the named inline properties on every node, reads every box and restores each value with its priority, in one task with no `await`. The plugin writes `height: rowHeight` on every item, as fixed mode does. It must NOT hardcode item anatomy, or answer post-transform rects that get written back as CSS lengths. Test isolation: a real-DOM arm, since only a real DOM tells the natural read from the written one.
*   **Patch Verdict:** Matches, and closes one gap I had not listed. The read answers the layout box (`getLayoutRect`), so a scaled ancestor cannot leak into a written height. `createItem`'s mode branch collapses to `rowHeight`, and `repositionItems` writes the same value in fixed mode, so there is no vdom delta. `properties` generalises to width at no cost.
*   **Premise Coherence:** Coheres with friction→gold: the first real consumer (Institution #128) surfaced the split, and the fix makes the mode serve that consumer by config. It coheres with verify-before-assert too: the freeze was found by a mutation, not reasoned.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge OR documented search (per guide §7.1):**

- **Challenge** (non-blocking, hypothesis — needs V-B-A before implementation): the ticket lists "an item whose own CSS transitions `height`" as option B's falsifier, and neither the method doc nor the body returns to it. My reading of where it can bite:
  - Releasing an inline height to `auto` cannot animate, because `auto` isn't interpolable, so the default case is safe.
  - An item whose CSS gives it a non-auto height (a %, a `calc()`, a token) *and* transitions `height` would start a transition on the release. A synchronous read in that task then reports the transition's start value, the old inline height, and the row freezes again.
  - A sentence in `getNaturalRect`'s JSDoc would keep the next consumer from walking into it. Suspending `transition` inside the same task would close it outright.
- **Documented search:** I also looked for these and found no concerns:
  - the plugin's own transitions touching `height`: its per-owner rule transitions only `opacity` and `transform`;
  - fixed mode changing: `rowHeight` is `owner.itemHeight` there, `createItem` writes the value it always wrote, and `repositionItems` rewrites the same value;
  - a released frame painting: no `await` and no timer between release and restore, and your arm reads the `!important` priority back unchanged.

### 🧠 Graph Ingestion Notes

*   **`[KB_GAP]`**: An element carrying an inline `height` answers every rect read with that value, so a size written from a measurement freezes every later measurement. It is not grow-only, and no guide said so. `DomAccess#getNaturalRect` is now the read that sidesteps it.
*   **`[TOOLING_GAP]`**: N/A
*   **`[RETROSPECTIVE]`**: The read a value is written from has to be immune to the write. Here that meant a release-read-restore in one task, and the layout box rather than the visual rect.
